data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet summarizes France’s performance and equity-related patterns using PISA 2022 results for 15-year-old students. It reports trends from 2018 to 2022 and longer-run comparisons (e.g., changes since 2012) across mathematics, reading and science, including proficiency-level shares (e.g., Level 2 baseline and Level 5/6 top performers) and gaps by socio-economic status and gender. For France, average performance is described as close to the OECD average in all three subjects, with declines in mathematics and reading relative to 2018 and the lowest-ever levels in all three subjects. The factsheet also reports that socio-economic status is a strong predictor of mathematics performance in France (accounting for 21% of variation), and provides descriptive results on immigrant background differences and school climate indicators. Because this is a descriptive reporting document rather than an ML study, no predictive model metrics, PV-handling procedures, or missing-data rules are specified in the text.
